title: Windowed simhash prefetcher for embedding cache with partial-match coalescing
creator: Ava Nguyen
description: Implement a windowed simhash-based prefetcher and partial-match coalescing layer for the embeddings KV cache to improve cold-start latency and reduce duplicate embedding computation. This ticket covers an end-to-end approach: compute compact simhash signatures on text inputs, maintain a sliding window LRU of recent signatures per-tenant (configurable window size), prefetch likely-hit embeddings asynchronously, and coalesce near-duplicate requests by returning cached embeddings or triggering a single upstream compute. The design emphasizes bounded memory, tenant isolation, and conservative false-positive avoidance so quality of reranking is preserved.
implementation_notes: Signature: 64-bit simhash derived from tokenized whitespace + normalized punctuation; canonicalization step strips stopwords for short inputs (<32 tokens)
Window: per-tenant ring buffer of recent N signatures (default N=2048). Eviction is strictly LRU within window; total memory capped per-tenant via config param.

Prefetch heuristic: when a new request's simhash H has Hamming distance <= 3 to any signature in window, schedule an async prefetch for the cached embedding id; prefetch rate limited to X req/s per tenant and subject to global burst budget.

Coalescing: dedupe table keyed by signature bucket (hash >> 4) with short TTL (default 2s) to coalesce concurrent near-duplicates; if an active in-flight compute exists, later requests subscribe to the same result stream.

Quality guardrails: only apply partial-match coalesce/prefetch for inputs with tokenized length >= 6 to avoid changing short prompt semantics; fallback to exact content-hash path for high-sensitivity customers.
Compatibility: integrate with existing embedding cache API; expose flags for runtime-1.21 rollout and per-tenant opt-out via config boolean.
Metrics: instrument hit-rate_by_hamming, prefetch_success_rate, coalesce_latency_savings_ms, false_positive_rate_estimate, and prefetch_cost_tokens.
Rollout plan: feature flag -> 1% tenants -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback if rerank-quality degradation > 1.5% on eval set.
Safety: ensure prefetch never returns stale embeddings beyond primary cache semantics; prefetch writes mark entries as 'prefetched' and don't override newer writes without CAS check.
updates: 2026-02-12: Scoping meeting complete. Decided on simhash due to low compute overhead and tunable Hamming threshold. Product asked for per-tenant opt-out and observability hooks.
2026-02-18: Prototype simhash generator implemented in Rust runtime shim. Microbenchmarks: simhash compute 0.5us/token on p3-standard; acceptable.

2026-02-25: End-to-end lab run with window N=2048: reduced cold-start QPS stall by 27% on synthetic rerank workload (95th p95 token-latency improvement 120ms). Qualitative review by ML team passed for 85% of sampled outputs.

2026-03-02: Design review notes from PM (Lena Patel): require explicit metric for rerank precision regression and an admin toggle in Console. Action: add prefetch_cost_tokens metric and Console toggle work item.

2026-03-08: Engineering review: replaced naive per-tenant Bloom filter with ring-buffer LRU after mem/CPU trade-off analysis. Update: reduced false-positive prefetches at cost of slightly higher memory but simpler invalidation.

2026-03-12: Development branch opened. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/2743. Integration tests added for race on coalesce table. Canary config prepared for runtime-1.21.
Next steps: complete integration tests for tenant isolation, add Console toggle, run 7-day canary against production-sampled traffic with eval harness to measure rerank precision.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end tests: coalesce subscribes and releases correctly under concurrency (unit + integration).
Measured p95 request latency improvement >= 80ms for cold-start slices on production-sampled rerank traffic during 10% canary (no more than 1% increase in end-to-end failures).
Prefetch cost tokens < configured budget (default 3% of token budget) during steady state.
No observed rerank precision regression > 1.5% on the evaluation suite after canary.
Console: per-tenant toggle exists and can force-disable feature; feature flagging works across Dedicated and Private deployments.
qa_notes: Simulate tenant with high duplication (search-autocomplete style) and verify coalesce reduces duplicate upstream compute.
Verify tenant isolation by running concurrent tenants with identical content and ensuring no cross-tenant cache leakage.
Introduce staleness scenarios: simulate a rewritten embedding upstream and ensure prefetch does not serve older embedding after a newer write.
Stress test coalesce table under 20k concurrent requests and assert latencies remain under SLOs.
